questions.sectionTitle: Module 2: Authentication, Cryptography & OWASP AppSec Checkpoint
questions.prompt: Why does trusting `req.body.userId` instead of verified session `auth().userId` create an immediate vulnerability?

options.text: Any attacker can forge any victim's `userId` inside JSON bodies and impersonate accounts freely
JSON bodies cannot parse UUID strings
It triggers syntax errors in TypeScript

questions.explanation: Authenticated subject identity must come strictly from verified server session tokens/cookies.

questions.sectionTitle: Module 2: Authentication, Cryptography & OWASP AppSec Checkpoint
questions.prompt: Why is Argon2id strictly recommended over raw SHA-256 for storing user password digests?

options.text: Argon2id consumes configurable memory and CPU work factor with unique salts, making GPU brute-force cracking orders of magnitude slower
SHA-256 outputs can be decoded straight back to strings via algebra
Argon2id removes the need for HTTPS
SHA-256 only hashes passwords shorter than 8 characters

questions.explanation: Fast hashes fail against GPU cracking farms; slow memory-hard functions defend user credentials cleanly.

questions.sectionTitle: Module 2: Authentication, Cryptography & OWASP AppSec Checkpoint
questions.prompt: What vulnerability allows Student A to view Student B's exam submission simply by requesting `/api/attempts/1002` instead of `1001`?
questions.explanation: Failing to enforce ownership per requested resource ID causes IDOR / BOLA.

questions.sectionTitle: Module 2: Authentication, Cryptography & OWASP AppSec Checkpoint
questions.prompt: Why do `HttpOnly` session cookies outperform `localStorage` tokens against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)?

options.text: `HttpOnly` cookies cannot be read via browser `document.cookie` JavaScript, stopping XSS payloads from exfiltrating the raw token

questions.explanation: Isolating credentials away from JS DOM scope blunts token theft.

questions.prompt: What happens if an attacker enters `' OR '1'='1` into an application using parameterized queries (`WHERE email = $1`)?

options.text: The database safely looks for an exact literal email matching `' OR '1'='1` and returns zero rows without running boolean OR logic
The attacker logs in automatically as Admin
Node throws an unhandled promise panic

questions.explanation: Parameterized variables are never parsed as SQL keywords or operators.
